rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods / Results (Figs 1-9) - the authors report their own laboratory incubations of two agricultural soils (loamy silt T1, sandy silt V1) measuring NO and N2O release by nitrification and denitrification under varying O2 partial pressures and soil moisture contents.
rows.notes: The study contains no irrigation treatment, no drip or subsurface drip system, and no crop yield or crop production measurement. It is a laboratory incubation (5-10 g soil in serum bottles, 25 C) on trace gas release. What it actually shows on the cited point is only that the fine-textured loamy silt showed higher N2O release by denitrification at 80-100% whc than the coarse-textured sandy silt, and the authors assume (not measure) that the fine-textured soil became anoxic at a lower moisture content (Discussion, Fig. 6). This is at most support for a precondition (poorer aeration in fine-textured soils) of the claimed subsurface drip yield advantage, not evidence on drip irrigation or crop production. Note that the review cites the paper as 2004, but the document is dated 1998.

notes: Full text appears complete (pages 387-396). The paper is a laboratory soil incubation study on NO/N2O emissions; it does not involve any irrigation technology or crop yield, so it cannot provide own evidence on the drip crop-production claim.
